codebook_ambiguities: The codebook says D9 support parks write no conflict_detection row. In this A2 run, 83 claims parked unsupported_by_span still have a conflict_detection noop row ('No positive claims; negative-only or empty'). It comes right after their claim_support_check and a resolution with claim_count 0, e.g. F09 i=741/742/743. Read literally, that later row is the 'last logged evaluation' and files the claim under a key, giving proposed/no_positive_claim_left instead of filed/cycle2_parked_unsupported_by_span. A rule is needed for which wins when a park and a noop row come from the same evaluation.

split_across_claims covers only claims with one subject. A compound value whose parts were extracted from the cited span under different subjects therefore falls into claims_without_the_value, which mixes 'value absent' with 'value split'. F82: 'selection method' average + pick best vs 'Antrecorp' rejected.

Parts versus qualifiers when a part of a compound value is itself another gold row. Examples: F82's Antrecorp exclusion is R06's value; F91's 'not as a third paper' is R08's value. The sibling rule says a sibling's value does not carry, but it does not say whether a text that leaves out the sibling part still carries the rest. I treated the F82 omission as a missing independent part, because the run's judge flagged it, and the F91 omission as an implied contrast.

Demoted rows: the codebook gives only the pass rule (no fact holding the value is current at k) and the still_current sub-code. It does not say whether the polarity/modality steps apply, or which modality is required when the value was a candidate before it was demoted (F36 carriers are proposed). It also does not say whether a current_unconfirmed fact counts as current; I assumed it does.

applied/proposal_expired takes the proposal's final status, not the cause. In F06 the proposal was raised in phase 0 and then expired after the claim was re-evaluated into A2 same-meeting conflicts, so the A2 same_meeting_conflict mechanism is invisible at 'proposed'. When a proposal from an earlier evaluation passes 'proposed', there is no rule for using the last evaluation's reason.

'The question is scored correct' does not say which scorer counts. The legacy 'correct' and 'state_layer.correct' disagree. Example: EL2020d_yesno_F82 is legacy False because the judge marked the Antrecorp part missing, but state_layer True with value_ok and the fact given.

Locating the cited span: some gold evidence lines are short back-channels that occur in many spans, e.g. EL2020c:300 'Yeah, yeah.' in about 20 spans. The codebook does not say to place the span by the distinctive evidence line(s) only.

Reading a fact with its key versus the plain text: in F53 the value text states the gold strategy, but the claim's subject/key file it as a Czech segmenter matter. 'Decide by its most common context' does not cover a text whose words state the value while its key narrows the scope.

codebook_ambiguities: Single-value reading questions: the codebook excludes rejected_so_far, citing its 2-8 values, but EL2020a_rejected_so_far asks for exactly one gold value (R01). It is unclear whether it counts as a single-value question at k=0. It did not matter here, because R01 fails before the reading steps.

Main decision versus minor qualifier is not defined for value shapes beyond the two examples. The verdict flips on this choice for F04 ('shared document' + 'one section per language'), F70 ('own GPU machines' + 'TPU only as a fallback') and to a small degree F85 ('listen to the sound' + 'the sound is the only ground truth').

split_across_claims requires the claims to share one subject. When a value is split across a near-identical subject pair (F04: 'document' versus '[ORGANIZATION3] document'), the codebook assigns claims_without_the_value, which hides an extraction split.

Ruled-out rows ('names the option'): it is unclear whether a text that names the act without the option's distinguishing qualifiers counts. R01: 'PERSON2 will send the document by tonight' names sending but not 'to the organiser' or 'by e-mail'.

Dating parking: a claim can be extracted in phase p, pass a filing_type_check in phase p without being parked, and be parked by a support check only in a later phase (R02: extracted in phase 1, parked in phase 2). At checkpoints between those phases it has no logged evaluation, and the codebook does not say which filed sub-code applies there (not_evaluated or no_key). claim_support_check rows also carry no claim_id, so joining them to claims by the reason text breaks if two claims share a reason.

Every claim is evaluated twice per phase and again in each later phase, sometimes under different keys. The proposed step matches 'a proposal or fact holding a carrier claim's value under the key that claim was evaluated under', but the codebook does not say which evaluation's key is meant when the keys differ.

Demoted rows: the codebook gives the outcomes (ok:demoted, ok:never_stored, still_current) but not what to report as the first failing step when the row passes, or whether the extraction and filing steps are traced at all for a demoted row. I reported 'passes' with ok:never_stored for F35.

same_meeting_conflict covers two different A2 reasons: 'rival values asserted in the same meeting' when the key has no current fact (F62), and 'rival challengers asserted in the same meeting' when it has one (F65). The codebook does not distinguish them.
Modality is read from the claim's modality field, not its predicate: carriers with the predicate 'considered' but modality 'asserted' (F62, F65) pass modality. The codebook leaves this implicit.

findings.title: The sibling rule ignores the sibling's own adjudication, so F06's verbatim gold value never reaches the queue
findings.location: 23-loss-trace.py Judge.level (theirs loop, ~l.704-708); queue construction in main (~l.1201-1220)
findings.claim: F38 has alias '42 languages', which is exactly F06's value. phrases() gives F38 an equal share of the text '42 languages', and the locality tie-break never applies because the fact value is not local to F06. So Judge(F06).level('42 languages') = 'weak' and verdict is (False, False). The adjudicator has already ruled '42 languages' false for F38 (adj_r12 F38: '42 languages': false), but level() still lets F38 claim its share. Because neither bound counts the text, it is never pending and never queued, so the primary series can be 'complete' without ever deciding it. Reproduction: in a0_r1 at k=1, a current_confirmed fact '42 languages' sits on person6.multilingual_model.language_count (it supersedes the adjudicated-true '42-language model'). The trace still codes F06 k1 as current/overwritten_by_non_gold_value with successor_values ['42 languages'], i.e. 'overwritten' by its own value. In el2020_a1_20261022T211107Z and a1_r3, '42 languages' is current_confirmed at k=1, yet F06 k1-3 is coded applied/proposal_expired. A verbatim-value cross-check over all nine runs finds only these F06 rows (F04 is correctly stopped at modality).
findings.estimated_rows_affected: 7 strict rows in both the adjudicated and raw series: a0_r1 F06 k1 (current/overwritten -> ok:stored_not_asked); el2020_a1 F06 k1 (applied/proposal_expired -> ok:stored_not_asked), k2 and k3 (-> current/displaced_by_other_gold_value); a1_r3 F06 k1-3 (same as el2020_a1). These are the outcomes once the text is decided true; the v3 judge reaches the same 7 rows once it has that decision.
findings.suggested_fix: In Judge.level, skip a sibling r for which adj[r['fact_id']].get(text) is False. With that patch, ('F06', '42 languages') enters the lenient queue, and only that item is added. Side effect to handle: the same patch frees F86's distinctive alias 'EAF' from R07, so three F86 k3 rows (a0_r2, a1_r3, a2_r2b) gain strict carriers ('EAF and OSTT files considered ...', etc.). Those texts land in the 'decides' queue and need adjudication. Alternatively, queue any text that matches the row as strong before the sibling rule when every sibling holding the blocking share has adjudicated it false.

findings.title: another_value_won when the 'winner' is the carrier claim's own value
findings.location: 23-loss-trace.py trace_row, carried_kv gate (~l.776-784) and the proposed-failure branch (~l.875-890)
findings.claim: For claims that carry the value only through subject+predicate+object, v3 propagates identity only when the key's words plus the value still match. When that gate fails, the claim's own proposal (same value, same key) is not credited. The proposed-failure branch then sees result 'reject' or 'new' with a proposal_id and codes another_value_won, although the winning value is the claim's own object. The winner also fails match_level, so it is not added to wording_pairs, and the pair never reaches the adjudicator. Reproduction a0_r1 R07 k3: claim b5e0e654 'OSTT files | rejected as correction basis | trusting OSTT for correctness' is negative, asserted, with its SPO adjudicated true. Its last evaluation (phase 3, key source_file.selected) raised a reject proposal 'trusting OSTT for correctness', which was accepted, and a REJECTED fact was created in phase 3. The trace says proposed/another_value_won with wording_pairs []. a2_r1 R06 k3 is the same shape: 'Antrecorp | rejected | dropped from consideration because it is very unstable' (SPO adjudicated true) raised its own accepted reject proposal.
findings.estimated_rows_affected: 10 strict rows in each series (adjudicated and raw): a0_r1 R05 k2, R05 k3, R07 k3; el2020_a1_20261022T211107Z R05 k2, R05 k3, R07 k3; a1_r2 F21 k1, F68 k2, R07 k3; a2_r1 R06 k3 (out of 142 / 129 another_value_won rows)
findings.suggested_fix: When a filed carrier's last evaluation raised a proposal whose _norm(value) equals the carrier's own _norm(_value(c)), do not code another_value_won. Use a distinct sub-code (e.g. own_value_not_matched) and add the proposal value to wording_pairs so the (key, value) pair is adjudicated. Or credit the claim's own proposal and fact under its own key whenever the claim text itself is adjudicated true.

findings.title: sibling_value_only is produced by claim-level adjudication, and split_across_claims has the same blind spot
findings.claim: claim_text makes a false decision on a claim's object decide the whole claim. The sibling_value_only test, however, checks each text separately ('t not in judge.adj'). An unadjudicated SPO of an adjudicated-false claim that the raw matcher rates strong is therefore reported as a sibling problem; no sibling is involved. Reproduction: F86 k3 in a0_r2, a1_r3 and a2_r2b is coded carried/sibling_value_only. The only strong local text is 'Flip a coin to choose between EAF and OSTT' (strong through alias 'choose the EAF'; adj F86: false), plus its unadjudicated SPO 'mismatch resolution rejected Flip a coin ...'. In the raw series there are 0 sibling_value_only rows. Skipping adjudicated claims in this test, as tested, moves a0_r2 and a2_r2b to split_across_claims. The join (subject 'mismatch resolution') matches only because its one raw-strong member is that same adjudicated-false text; the other members ('Use mismatches to locate spots and re-listen to the sound', 'sound to resolve mismatches by re-listening') match nothing. The 18 current split_across_claims rows (F23) are legitimate: each fragment is raw-weak and adjudicated false individually.
findings.estimated_rows_affected: 3 strict rows (adjudicated series): a0_r2, a1_r3, a2_r2b F86 k3. The correct code is claims_without_the_value; boundary unchanged.
findings.suggested_fix: In the sibling_value_only test, skip a claim if any of its texts ({_value(c), _spo(c)}) is in judge.adj. In split_across_claims, drop members whose texts are adjudicated false, and require that no single member text matches strong on its own.

findings.title: Codebook still describes v2 in the chain table and flags
findings.claim: Mismatches between the codebook and v3 code. (a) filed/no_key says '(no key or the literal key `null`)'; v3 files 'null' keys. In A0, 'null' keys do raise accepted proposals and facts (a0_r1: 18 trail rows, 4 facts; a0_r2: 25, 7; a0_r3: 2, 2). In A1/A2 they are noop 'bug 5' rows, coded undefined_key. So the code is right and the table is wrong. (b) applied lists applied_after_checkpoint, which v3 removed. That is safe here because value_policy is structural: a proposal is accepted at the checkpoint it was raised or never. The replay dates a fact by its proposal's raise phase, which would be wrong under the gold_backed policy. (c) current lists not_current, which is unreachable (the code says so). (d) split_across_claims is described as 'claims from the cited span that share a subject'; the code uses the whole window (cited span ±1) and judge.level (with the sibling rule), and any polarity or modality. (e) sibling_value_only is missing from the table. (f) displaced_by_other_gold_value is defined as 'a later fact on the key ... holds another gold value'; v3 decides on the immediate successor only and records later_gold_in_chain (16 adjudicated rows carry it, 15 of them coded overwritten). (g) credit_without_state is described as '(a loss at any step before answered)'. v3 evaluates it per question, so it can be true at answered: a1_r3 F85 k3 is answered/answer_or_judge with credit_without_state=true, because EL2020d_cs_F85 was scored correct without the fact while EL2020d_yesno_F85 got the fact and was scored wrong.
findings.estimated_rows_affected: 0 count changes; affects how 231+ coded rows are read (e.g. 139 overwritten, 20 displaced, 16 credit_without_state in the adjudicated series)
findings.suggested_fix: Update the table: 'null' is filed in A0 and coded undefined_key under the bug-5 repair; drop applied_after_checkpoint and not_current (or mark them unreachable under the structural policy); redefine split_across_claims; add sibling_value_only; describe immediate-successor displacement and later_gold_in_chain; restate credit_without_state per question.

findings.title: Codebook matcher, locality and adjudication sections do not describe v3 (distinctive-alias upgrade acts in the strict bound)
findings.claim: Undocumented v3 behaviour. (1) The one-word upgrade is described under 'Lenient bound' only, and only for one-word values. In code it lives in Judge.level, so it creates strict passes, and v3 extends it to 'distinctive' one-word aliases: MP3, 42, ASR, ELAN, Czech, English, French, German, 21, 32%, 3, 'the 3', EAF, Google, Microsoft, Antrecorp, 23rd, Romanian, Bosnian/Croatian/Serbian/Montenegrin. Against adj_r12, occurrences where the upgrade alone made a local text strong were adjudicated 27 true vs 121 false (109 undecided). Disabling it moves 54 raw strict rows (22 boundaries) and 5 adjudicated rows (a2_r2b F67 k2-3, a2_r3 F20 k1-3). (2) Not documented: the shared-evidence sibling exemption, the locality tie-break for equal shares, phrases() always adding the covered part, aliases needing a phrase window (_near), the 'one' exclusion from required numbers, and the stemmer's undoubling and irregulars. (3) 'A proposal or fact holding a carrier claim's value ... carries the value too': v3 restricts this to object-carrying claims, or a key+value match at any level (weak suffices: requiring strong moves 17 rows, F31 in five runs and F70 in a2_r1). (4) Not documented: claim-level adjudication, holds() checking adjudications first, the queue now holding every strict-deciding support text per step, primary_series_complete, and the arm-label rule (A2 requires all four contracts, else 'mixed'). (5) The verification table cites 7 runs; I re-ran it on all 9 (answer-fact status vs status_at, and currency on resolved keys) with 0 mismatches. (6) The alias_collisions docstring says the sibling rule separates the listed pairs; F26/F27, F61/R04, F70/R05, F82/R06 and F91/R08 share evidence and are exempt.
findings.estimated_rows_affected: Raw strict: 54 rows rest on the distinctive upgrade alone, 17 on the weak propagation gate. Primary series: unaffected once the queue is adjudicated.
